source.text: Προσέχετε δὲ τὴν δικαιοσύνην ὑμῶν μὴ ποιεῖν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ἀνθρώπων πρὸς τὸ θεαθῆναι αὐτοῖς· εἰ δὲ μή γε, μισθὸν οὐκ ἔχετε παρὰ τῷ πατρὶ ὑμῶν τῷ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Beware then the righteousness of you not to do before the men in order to be seen by them; if but not indeed, reward not you have with the Father of you the in the heavens.

en.L: But be careful not to do your righteousness before {{gender:people|men}} in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father who [is] in the heavens.
en.B: Take care not to put your righteousness on show for others to see. If you do, your Father in heaven has no reward for you.
en.R: Be careful! When you do what is righteous, do not do it in front of people just so they will see you. If you do, you will get no reward from your Father in heaven.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} cuidado de no practicar {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} justicia delante de {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} para ser vistos por ellos; de lo contrario, no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} recompensa de parte de {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que [está] en los cielos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado de no hacer alarde de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} justicia para que los demás {{plural_you:los|os}} vean. Si lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo no tendrá recompensa para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} cuidado! Cuando {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} lo que es justo, no lo {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}} delante de la gente solo para que {{plural_you:los|os}} vean. Si lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo no {{plural_you:les|os}} dará ninguna recompensa.

sw.L: Lakini jihadharini msitende haki yenu mbele ya watu ili mwonwe nao; la sivyo, hamna ujira kwa Baba yenu aliye katika mbingu.
sw.B: Jihadharini msiionyeshe haki yenu hadharani ili watu wawaone. Mkifanya hivyo, Baba yenu wa mbinguni hatakuwa na ujira kwa ajili yenu.
sw.R: Jihadharini! Mnapotenda yaliyo haki, msiyatende mbele ya watu ili tu wawaone. Mkifanya hivyo, hamtapata ujira wowote kutoka kwa Baba yenu aliye mbinguni.

decisions.choice: righteousness: acts of devotion to God
decisions.reason: Here righteousness is the practice of piety. The three examples follow: giving to the poor (6:2-4), prayer (6:5-15) and fasting (6:16-18).

decisions.choice: in order to be seen by them: the purpose is the problem, not being seen
alternatives: never doing good where others can see
decisions.reason: Jesus has told his disciples to let their good deeds be seen so that God is glorified (5:16). What he forbids is doing them for one's own praise.

decisions.choice: righteousness, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: alms, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have "alms" here, the word of 6:2. Early manuscripts have "righteousness". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural 'you' ({{plural_you:tengan|tened}}, {{plural_you:su|vuestra}})
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the crowd, so each plural "you", pronoun or verb, is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain). Where he speaks to one listener, as in verses 2-4, 6 and 17-18, Spanish uses "tú", which has no setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has the same two wordings as English here, "la gente" or "los hombres" in the older sense of human beings, so Literal keeps the gender setting, as in verses 2, 5, 14-16 and 18. Balanced and Readable say "los demás" and "la gente".

decisions.choice: haki yenu (L, B); yaliyo haki (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for righteousness. Here it means acts of devotion to God (meaning decision m1), the giving, praying and fasting of verses 2-18; "haki" keeps the link with 5:20, where the same word is used.

decisions.choice: ujira
decisions.reason: As in 5:46: the Greek word is a wage, and "ujira" carries the picture of being "paid in full" in verses 2, 5 and 16; "thawabu" is the familiar religious word for reward.

source.text: Ὅταν οὖν ποιῇς ἐλεημοσύνην, μὴ σαλπίσῃς ἔμπροσθέν σου, ὥσπερ οἱ ὑποκριταὶ ποιοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς ῥύμαις, ὅπως δοξασθῶσιν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: When therefore you do alms, not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by the men; truly I say to you, they have the reward of them.

en.L: So when you give alms, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be glorified by {{gender:people|men}}. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full.
en.B: So when you give to the poor, do not announce it with trumpets, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and on the streets to win praise from others. Truly I tell you, they have already been paid in full.
en.R: So when you give money to people in need, do not make a big show of it. The hypocrites do that in the synagogues and on the streets, so that people will praise them. I tell you the truth, the praise they get is all the reward they will ever have.

es.L: Por tanto, cuando des limosna, no toques la trompeta delante de ti, tal como los hipócritas hacen en las sinagogas y en los callejones, a fin de ser glorificados por {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: ya tienen cobrada su recompensa.
es.B: Así que, cuando ayudes a los pobres, no lo anuncies a son de trompeta, como hacen los hipócritas en las sinagogas y en las calles para ganarse los elogios de los demás. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ya han recibido toda su paga.
es.R: Así que, cuando des dinero a los necesitados, no hagas un gran espectáculo. Eso es lo que hacen los hipócritas en las sinagogas y en las calles, para que la gente los alabe. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: los elogios que reciben son toda la recompensa que van a tener.

sw.L: Basi, unapotoa sadaka, usipige tarumbeta mbele yako, kama wanafiki wanavyofanya katika masinagogi na katika vichochoro, ili watukuzwe na watu. Kweli nawaambia, wamekwisha kupokea ujira wao wote.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo unapowapa maskini msaada, usitangaze kwa tarumbeta, kama wanafiki wanavyofanya katika masinagogi na barabarani ili wasifiwe na watu. Kweli nawaambia, wamekwisha kulipwa kikamilifu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo unapowapa wahitaji pesa, usijionyeshe mbele ya watu. Wanafiki hufanya hivyo katika masinagogi na barabarani ili watu wawasifu. Nawaambia ukweli: sifa wanazopata ndizo ujira wote watakaopata.

decisions.choice: alms: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a central duty of Jewish piety (Deuteronomy 15:11; Tobit 12:8).

decisions.choice: do not sound a trumpet: do not draw attention to your giving
alternatives: a literal trumpet blown at the time of giving
decisions.reason: No source shows that trumpets were blown when alms were given. The phrase is a picture of self-advertisement.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus uses it of those whose religious acts are done for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 23:13-29).

decisions.choice: be glorified: be praised by people
decisions.reason: The verb usually speaks of giving glory to God. Here it is the praise of people, which is what the hypocrites seek.

decisions.choice: they have their reward: they have been paid in full, and there is nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: "received in full". The praise of people is the whole of their reward.

decisions.choice: win praise (B); praise them (R)
decisions.reason: The key term "glorify" is used of honor given to God. Here the honor is human, so Balanced and Readable say "praise", as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The wording for Jesus's single "amen" throughout Matthew, as in John. The same in verses 5 and 16.

decisions.choice: ya tienen cobrada su recompensa (L); ya han recibido toda su paga (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one written on a receipt: paid in full (meaning decision m5). "Cobrar" and "paga" keep that picture of a settled account.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The wording for Jesus's single "amen" throughout Matthew, as in John. The same in verses 5 and 16.

source.text: σοῦ δὲ ποιοῦντος ἐλεημοσύνην μὴ γνώτω ἡ ἀριστερά σου τί ποιεῖ ἡ δεξιά σου, ὅπως ᾖ σου ἡ ἐλεημοσύνη ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.

records.literal_gloss: Of you then doing alms not let know the left of you what does the right of you, \v 4 so that may be your the alms in the secret; and the Father of you the seeing in the secret will repay you.

en.L: But when you give alms, do not let your left [hand] know what your right is doing, \v 4 so that your alms may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
en.B: But when you give, keep it so quiet that your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing. \v 4 Your gift will be hidden, and your Father, who sees what is hidden, will repay you.
en.R: But when you give to someone in need, do it so quietly that even your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing. \v 4 Give in secret. Your Father sees what you do in secret, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reward you.

es.L: Pero tú, al dar limosna, no dejes que tu [mano] izquierda sepa qué hace tu derecha, \v 4 de modo que tu limosna quede en lo oculto; y tu Padre, que ve en lo oculto, te recompensará.
es.B: Tú, en cambio, cuando des, hazlo tan en silencio que tu mano izquierda no sepa lo que hace tu mano derecha. \v 4 Tu donativo quedará escondido, y tu Padre, que ve lo escondido, te lo pagará.
es.R: Pero cuando ayudes a alguien necesitado, hazlo tan calladamente que ni siquiera tu mano izquierda sepa lo que hace tu mano derecha. \v 4 Da en secreto. Tu Padre ve lo que haces en secreto, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te recompensará.

sw.L: Lakini wewe, ukitoa sadaka, usiuache [mkono] wako wa kushoto ujue kile ule wa kulia unachofanya, \v 4 ili sadaka yako ifanyike kwa siri; na Baba yako, anayeona yaliyo sirini, atakulipa.
sw.B: Lakini wewe unapotoa, fanya kimya kimya hivi kwamba mkono wako wa kushoto usijue kile ambacho mkono wa kulia unafanya. \v 4 Msaada wako utabaki umefichika, na Baba yako, anayeona yaliyofichika, atakulipa.
sw.R: Lakini unapompa mhitaji msaada, fanya hivyo kwa utulivu kiasi kwamba hata mkono wako wa kushoto usijue mkono wako wa kulia unafanya nini. \v 4 Toa kwa siri. Baba yako huona unachofanya kwa siri, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakupa ujira.

decisions.choice: left hand, right hand: give without fuss, without even dwelling on it yourself
alternatives: keep it from your closest friend
decisions.reason: The overstatement says the giving should be so quiet that it is hidden even from oneself.

decisions.choice: your Father who sees in secret will reward you: God sees and gives what he has promised
alternatives: a wage earned by the act
decisions.reason: What is done for God alone is seen by him. The reward is his gift, in this life and at the last day (6:20; 25:34-40).

decisions.choice: will reward you, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: will reward you openly, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "openly" here and in 6:6 and 6:18. Early manuscripts lack it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: Καὶ ὅταν προσεύχησθε, οὐκ ἔσεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταί· ὅτι φιλοῦσιν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ ἐν ταῖς γωνίαις τῶν πλατειῶν ἑστῶτες προσεύχεσθαι, ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσι τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And when you pray, not you will be as the hypocrites; for they love in the synagogues and in the corners of the wide streets standing to pray, so that they may be seen by the men; truly I say to you, they have the reward of them.

en.L: And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and on the corners of the wide streets, so that they may be seen by {{gender:people|men}}. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full.
en.B: And when you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand and pray in the synagogues and at the street corners where others can see them. Truly I tell you, they have been paid in full.
en.R: When you pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand up and pray in the synagogues and on street corners, so that people will see them. I tell you the truth, that is all the reward they will get.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, no {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} como los hipócritas, porque a ellos les gusta orar de pie en las sinagogas y en las esquinas de las avenidas, para dejarse ver por {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: ya tienen cobrada su recompensa.
es.B: Y cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, no {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} como los hipócritas. A ellos les encanta orar de pie en las sinagogas y en las esquinas de las calles, donde todos los vean. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ya han recibido toda su paga.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, no {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} como los hipócritas. A ellos les gusta orar de pie en las sinagogas y en las esquinas, para que la gente los vea. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: esa es toda la recompensa que van a recibir.

sw.L: Na mnapoomba, hamtakuwa kama wanafiki; kwa sababu wanapenda kusimama na kuomba katika masinagogi na katika pembe za barabara kuu, ili waonekane na watu. Kweli nawaambia, wamekwisha kupokea ujira wao wote.
sw.B: Na mnapoomba, msiwe kama wanafiki. Wao hupenda kusimama na kuomba katika masinagogi na kwenye pembe za barabara, mahali ambapo watu wanaweza kuwaona. Kweli nawaambia, wamekwisha kulipwa kikamilifu.
sw.R: Mnapoomba, msiwe kama wanafiki. Wanapenda kusimama na kuomba katika masinagogi na kwenye pembe za barabara, ili watu wawaone. Nawaambia ukweli: huo ndio ujira wote watakaopata.

decisions.choice: standing to pray at the street corners: praying where the most people pass
alternatives: a rule that prayer must be in private
decisions.reason: Jews stood to pray, at set hours of the day. Someone who was out when the hour came could stop where he was; the hypocrites make sure that is at a busy corner.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus uses it of those whose religious acts are done for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 23:13-29).

decisions.choice: they have their reward: they have been paid in full, and there is nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: "received in full". The praise of people is the whole of their reward.

source.text: σὺ δὲ ὅταν προσεύχῃ, εἴσελθε εἰς τὸ ταμεῖόν σου καὶ κλείσας τὴν θύραν σου πρόσευξαι τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυπτῷ ἀποδώσει σοι.

records.literal_gloss: You but when you pray, go into the inner room of you and having shut the door of you pray to the Father of you the in the secret; and the Father of you the seeing in the secret will repay you.

en.L: But you, when you pray, go into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who [is] in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
en.B: But when you pray, go into an inner room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is there in secret. Your Father sees what is hidden, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay you.
en.R: But when you pray, go into a room by yourself and shut the door. Pray to your Father. He is there with you, though no one can see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Your Father sees what you do in secret, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reward you.

es.L: Pero tú, cuando ores, entra en tu cuarto interior y, después de cerrar tu puerta, ora a tu Padre que [está] en lo oculto; y tu Padre, que ve en lo oculto, te recompensará.
es.B: Tú, en cambio, cuando ores, entra en un cuarto interior, cierra la puerta y ora a tu Padre, que está allí en lo escondido. Tu Padre ve lo escondido, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te lo pagará.
es.R: Pero cuando ores, entra en un cuarto donde estés solo y cierra la puerta. Ora a tu Padre. Él está allí contigo, aunque nadie {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vea. Tu Padre ve lo que haces en secreto, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te recompensará.

sw.L: Wewe lakini, unapoomba, ingia ndani ya chumba chako cha faragha, na baada ya kufunga mlango wako, mwombe Baba yako aliye mahali pa siri; na Baba yako, anayeona yaliyo sirini, atakulipa.
sw.B: Lakini unapoomba, ingia katika chumba cha ndani, ufunge mlango, umwombe Baba yako aliye pale kwa siri. Baba yako huona yaliyofichika, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakulipa.
sw.R: Lakini unapoomba, ingia chumbani peke yako, ufunge mlango. Mwombe Baba yako. Yeye yuko pamoja nawe, ingawa hakuna anayeweza kumwona. Baba yako huona unachofanya kwa siri, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakupa ujira.

decisions.choice: inner room: a storeroom, the one room in a house with a door that shut
decisions.reason: Most houses had one main room; the storeroom was the place where one could be alone.

decisions.choice: you, singular: each one's own prayer
decisions.reason: The address changes to the singular. Jesus is not forbidding public prayer, which the Lord's Prayer itself assumes ("our Father"), but prayer made for show.

decisions.choice: your Father who sees in secret will reward you: God sees and gives what he has promised
alternatives: a wage earned by the act
decisions.reason: What is done for God alone is seen by him. The reward is his gift, in this life and at the last day (6:20; 25:34-40).

decisions.choice: chumba chako cha faragha
decisions.reason: The room was a storeroom, the one room in a house with a door that shut (meaning decision m1). "Chumba cha faragha" (private room) says why Jesus names it; Balanced says "chumba cha ndani" (inner room), as the English does.

source.text: Προσευχόμενοι δὲ μὴ βατταλογήσητε ὥσπερ οἱ ἐθνικοί, δοκοῦσιν γὰρ ὅτι ἐν τῇ πολυλογίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσακουσθήσονται·

records.literal_gloss: Praying but not babble as the Gentiles, they think for that in the many words of them they will be heard;

en.L: And when praying, do not babble like the Gentiles, for they think that in their many words they will be heard.
en.B: When you pray, do not keep piling up empty words as the pagans do. They think they will be heard because they say so much.
en.R: When you pray, do not keep saying words that mean nothing, like people who do not know God. They think they will be heard if they use a lot of words.

es.L: Y al orar, no {{plural_you:parloteen|parloteéis}} como los gentiles, pues piensan que en su mucho hablar serán escuchados.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, no {{plural_you:amontonen|amontonéis}} palabras vacías como hacen los gentiles. Ellos creen que serán escuchados por hablar mucho.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, no {{plural_you:repitan|repitáis}} palabras sin sentido, como la gente que no conoce a Dios. Esa gente cree que será escuchada si usa muchas palabras.

sw.L: Na mkiomba, msibwabwaje kama watu wa mataifa, kwa maana wanadhani kwamba katika wingi wa maneno yao watasikiwa.
sw.B: Mnapoomba, msirundike maneno matupu kama watu wa mataifa wanavyofanya. Wao hudhani kwamba watasikiwa kwa sababu wanasema mengi.
sw.R: Mnapoomba, msiendelee kusema maneno yasiyo na maana, kama watu wasiomjua Mungu. Wao hufikiri kwamba watasikiwa wakitumia maneno mengi.

decisions.choice: babble: pile up words without meaning
decisions.reason: The verb is rare and seems to imitate meaningless sounds. Pagan prayers often listed many names of gods and repeated formulas to make sure of being heard. Jesus himself prayed the same words more than once (26:44).

decisions.choice: the Gentiles: pagans, who did not know the God of Israel
decisions.reason: As in 5:47.

decisions.choice: msibwabwaje
decisions.reason: The verb means to pile up words without meaning (meaning decision m1), and it sounds like babbling. "Kubwabwaja" (to babble) has the same sound and sense.

source.text: μὴ οὖν ὁμοιωθῆτε αὐτοῖς, οἶδεν γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὧν χρείαν ἔχετε πρὸ τοῦ ὑμᾶς αἰτῆσαι αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Not therefore be like them, knows for the Father of you of what need you have before the you to ask him.

en.L: So do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: So do not imitate them. Your Father already knows what you need before you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Do not be like them. Your Father knows what you need even before you ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: No {{plural_you:se asemejen|os asemejéis}}, pues, a ellos, porque {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre sabe lo que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} antes de que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}}.
es.B: Así que no los {{plural_you:imiten|imitéis}}. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} Padre ya sabe lo que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} antes de que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} nada.
es.R: No {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} como ellos. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} Padre sabe lo que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}} aun antes de que {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} {{plural_you:pidan|pidáis}} algo.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo msiwe kama wao, kwa kuwa Baba yenu anafahamu mambo mnayoyahitaji kabla ninyi hamjamwomba.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiwaige. Baba yenu anajua tayari mnachohitaji kabla hamjamwomba.
sw.R: Msiwe kama wao. Baba yenu anajua mnachohitaji hata kabla hamjamwomba.

decisions.choice: your Father knows: prayer does not inform God or wear him down
alternatives: there is no need to pray
decisions.reason: Jesus still teaches his disciples to ask (6:9-13; 7:7-11). They pray as children to a Father who already cares, not to persuade a reluctant god.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on hamjamwomba (before you ask him)
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the object prefix -m- of the verb, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives (naye, lako, wako, yako in this passage). Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English here.

source.text: Οὕτως οὖν προσεύχεσθε ὑμεῖς· Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς· ἁγιασθήτω τὸ ὄνομά σου, ἐλθέτω ἡ βασιλεία σου, γενηθήτω τὸ θέλημά σου, ὡς ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς·

records.literal_gloss: Thus therefore pray you: Father of us the in the heavens, let be made holy the name of you; \v 10 let come the kingdom of you; let be done the will of you, as in heaven also on earth;

en.L: So pray like this: 'Our Father who [is] in the heavens, let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be made holy; \v 10 let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come; let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth;
en.B: So this is how you should pray: 'Our Father in heaven, may {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name be kept holy. \v 10 May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come. May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} will be done on earth, as it is done in heaven.
en.R: So when you pray, pray like this: 'Our Father in heaven, may everyone honor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name as holy. \v 10 May {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} kingdom come. May people on earth do what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, just as it is done in heaven.

es.L: Así, pues, {{plural_you:oren|orad}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}: “Padre nuestro que [estás] en los cielos, sea santificado {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre; \v 10 venga {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino; sea hecha {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voluntad, como en [el] cielo, también sobre [la] tierra;
es.B: Así es como {{plural_you:deben|debéis}} orar: “Padre nuestro que estás en el cielo, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre sea tenido por santo. \v 10 Que venga {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino. Que se haga {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} voluntad en la tierra, como se hace en el cielo.
es.R: Así que, cuando {{plural_you:oren|oréis}}, {{plural_you:oren|orad}} de esta manera: “Padre nuestro que estás en el cielo, que todos honren {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nombre como santo. \v 10 Que venga {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} reino. Que la gente en la tierra haga lo que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} quieres, así como se hace en el cielo.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo ninyi ombeni namna hii: 'Baba yetu uliye katika mbingu, jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} litakaswe; \v 10 ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} uje; mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} yafanyike, kama mbinguni, vivyo hivyo duniani;
sw.B: Basi ombeni hivi: 'Baba yetu wa mbinguni, jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} lihesabiwe kuwa takatifu. \v 10 Ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na uje. Mapenzi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na yatendeke duniani kama yanavyotendeka mbinguni.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo mnapoomba, ombeni hivi: 'Baba yetu uliye mbinguni, watu wote waliheshimu jina {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} kuwa takatifu. \v 10 Ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} na uje. Watu wa duniani wafanye yale {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unayoyataka, kama yanavyofanyika mbinguni.

decisions.choice: Our Father in heaven: God addressed with a child's trust and with reverence
decisions.reason: Jesus calls God Father and teaches his disciples to do the same. "In heaven" keeps his greatness in view.

decisions.choice: let your name be made holy: may God show his holiness, and may all honor it
alternatives: only a wish that people respect God
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself. The passive asks God to act so that his name is treated as holy (Ezekiel 36:23), and includes the honor his people give it.

decisions.choice: as in heaven, so on earth: may cover all three requests
alternatives: only the request about God's will
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the third request but may belong to all three: God's name, kingdom and will, honored on earth as in heaven.

decisions.choice: you: emphatic, you my disciples, unlike the pagans
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, setting the disciples' prayer against 6:7-8.

decisions.choice: your, you for God, with deity_pronoun spans
decisions.reason: The prayer speaks to God, so "your" and "you" take the usual span.

decisions.choice: may your name be kept holy (B); may everyone honor your name as holy (R)
decisions.reason: "Hallowed" is no longer current English. Balanced keeps the passive; Readable says who honors the name.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:oren|orad}} {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}
decisions.reason: The Greek adds an emphatic "you" (meaning decision m4): you, my disciples, unlike the pagans. Spanish does not need the pronoun, so Literal keeps it to show the emphasis; Balanced and Readable leave it in the verb.

decisions.choice: litakaswe (L); lihesabiwe kuwa takatifu (B); waliheshimu kuwa takatifu (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to make or treat as holy (meaning decision m2). "Kutakasa" is to make holy, and Balanced and Readable say "to be counted" and "to be honored" as holy, as the English does; "kutukuza" is to glorify, the verb of 6:2, and would blur the two.

source.text: τὸν ἄρτον ἡμῶν τὸν ἐπιούσιον δὸς ἡμῖν σήμερον·

records.literal_gloss: The bread of us the daily give us today;

en.L: Give us today our daily bread;
en.B: Give us today the bread we need.
en.R: Give us the food we need for today.

es.B: Danos hoy el pan que necesitamos.
es.R: Danos la comida que necesitamos para hoy.

sw.L: Mkate wetu wa kila siku utupe leo;

decisions.choice: daily: the bread needed for this day or the coming one
alternatives: the bread we need to live
decisions.reason: The word is found almost nowhere outside the Lord's Prayer, and its meaning is uncertain. It may mean "for the coming day" or "needed for life". Either way the request is for what is needed now, as God gave manna day by day (Exodus 16:4).

decisions.choice: food
decisions.reason: Bread stands for food in general. Readable says so.

source.text: καὶ ἄφες ἡμῖν τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν, ὡς καὶ ἡμεῖς ἀφήκαμεν τοῖς ὀφειλέταις ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: and forgive us the debts of us, as also we forgave the debtors of us;

en.L: and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors;
en.B: Forgive us what we owe {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, as we too have forgiven those who owe us.
en.R: Forgive us for the wrong things we have done, as we have forgiven people who have done wrong to us.

es.L: y perdónanos nuestras deudas, así como también nosotros hemos perdonado a los que nos deben;
es.B: Perdónanos lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} debemos, como también nosotros hemos perdonado a los que nos deben.
es.R: Perdónanos por las cosas malas que hemos hecho, así como nosotros hemos perdonado a los que nos han hecho mal.

sw.L: na utusamehe madeni yetu, kama vile sisi pia tumewasamehe wenye madeni kwetu;
sw.B: Utusamehe deni tunalodaiwa {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}, kama sisi pia tumewasamehe wale wanaodaiwa nasi.
sw.R: Utusamehe mabaya tuliyotenda, kama sisi tumewasamehe watu waliotutendea mabaya.

decisions.choice: debts: sins, as what we owe God
decisions.reason: In Aramaic the word for debt was also used of sin. Luke has "sins" (Luke 11:4), and Jesus speaks of "trespasses" in 6:14-15.

decisions.choice: as we have forgiven: those who ask forgiveness have already forgiven others
alternatives: a payment that earns God's forgiveness
decisions.reason: The past tense says the one who prays has already let others off. 6:14-15 and the parable in 18:23-35 show that God's forgiveness makes forgivers of those who receive it.

decisions.choice: what we owe you, with a deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of debt and says to whom it is owed.

decisions.choice: deni tunalodaiwa {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}
decisions.reason: The English Balanced says "what we owe you", with a deity_pronoun span on "you". Swahili says "the debt we are owed by you" with the free pronoun "nawe", which carries the span.

source.text: καὶ μὴ εἰσενέγκῃς ἡμᾶς εἰς πειρασμόν, ἀλλὰ ῥῦσαι ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ πονηροῦ.

records.literal_gloss: and not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil.

en.L: and do not bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one.'
en.B: And do not lead us into testing, but rescue us from the evil one.'
en.R: Do not bring us into times of testing. Save us from the evil one.'

es.L: y no nos introduzcas en tentación, sino rescátanos del maligno”.
es.B: Y no nos hagas entrar en la prueba, sino rescátanos del maligno”.
es.R: No nos lleves a tiempos de prueba. Sálvanos del maligno”.

sw.L: na usituingize katika jaribu, bali utuokoe kutoka kwa yule mwovu.'
sw.B: Usitulete katika majaribu, bali utuokoe kutoka kwa yule mwovu.'
sw.R: Usitupeleke katika nyakati za majaribu. Utuokoe kutoka kwa yule mwovu.'

decisions.choice: temptation: testing, a trial that could lead to falling away
decisions.reason: The word covers both a test of faith and an enticement to sin. God is not the one who tempts to sin (James 1:13); the request asks him to keep his children from trials they could not stand, as Jesus tells his disciples to pray in 26:41.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: As in 5:37, the form can be masculine or neuter. The tempter of 4:1-11 is the likely sense.

decisions.choice: the prayer ends here, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: with "For yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory for ever. Amen." added, in many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: The closing words of praise are not in the earliest manuscripts. They were added in the church's use of the prayer, following a pattern like 1 Chronicles 29:11. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: testing (B); times of testing (R)
decisions.reason: "Temptation" in English means only enticement to sin. Balanced and Readable use the wider word; Literal keeps the traditional one.

decisions.choice: del maligno
decisions.reason: The words can mean "evil" in general or "the evil one", the devil (meaning decision m2, uncertain). The English says "the evil one", and "el maligno" is the book-wide Spanish for that title; the familiar Spanish prayer says "líbranos del mal".

source.text: ἐὰν γὰρ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τὰ παραπτώματα αὐτῶν, ἀφήσει καὶ ὑμῖν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ οὐράνιος·

records.literal_gloss: If for you forgive the men the trespasses of them, will forgive also you the Father of you the heavenly;

en.L: For if you forgive {{gender:people|men}} their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you,
en.B: For if you forgive others when they wrong you, your Father in heaven will forgive you as well.
en.R: If you forgive people the wrong things they have done to you, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.

es.L: Porque si {{plural_you:perdonan|perdonáis}} a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} sus faltas, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre celestial {{plural_you:los|os}} perdonará también a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}},
es.B: Porque si {{plural_you:perdonan|perdonáis}} a los demás cuando {{plural_you:les|os}} ofenden, también {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo {{plural_you:los|os}} perdonará a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Si {{plural_you:perdonan|perdonáis}} a la gente el mal que {{plural_you:les|os}} han hecho, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre que está en el cielo también {{plural_you:los|os}} perdonará.

sw.L: Kwa kuwa ikiwa mnawasamehe watu makosa yao, Baba yenu wa mbinguni atawasamehe nanyi pia;
sw.B: Kwa maana mkiwasamehe wengine wanapowakosea, Baba yenu wa mbinguni atawasamehe ninyi pia.
sw.R: Mkiwasamehe watu mabaya waliyowatendea, Baba yenu aliye mbinguni atawasamehe ninyi pia.

decisions.choice: trespasses: wrongs, false steps
decisions.reason: The word means a stepping aside from the right way. It explains the "debts" of 6:12.

decisions.choice: forgiving and being forgiven belong together
alternatives: God's forgiveness is earned by forgiving
decisions.reason: Jesus comments on one request of the prayer. Those who will not forgive show they have not received God's mercy (18:32-35).

source.text: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἀφῆτε τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: if but not you forgive the men, neither the Father of you will forgive the trespasses of you.

en.L: but if you do not forgive {{gender:people|men}}, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
en.B: But if you refuse to forgive others, your Father will not forgive your wrongs either.
en.R: But if you do not forgive other people, your Father will not forgive the wrong things you have done.

es.L: pero si no {{plural_you:perdonan|perdonáis}} a {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}, tampoco {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre perdonará {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} faltas.
es.B: Pero si {{plural_you:se niegan|os negáis}} a perdonar a los demás, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre tampoco {{plural_you:les|os}} perdonará {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} faltas.
es.R: Pero si no {{plural_you:perdonan|perdonáis}} a los demás, {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre no {{plural_you:les|os}} perdonará el mal que {{plural_you:han|habéis}} hecho.

sw.L: lakini ikiwa hamwasamehi watu, hata Baba yenu hatayasamehe makosa yenu.
sw.B: Lakini mkikataa kuwasamehe wengine, Baba yenu naye hatawasamehe makosa yenu.
sw.R: Lakini msipowasamehe watu wengine, Baba yenu hatawasamehe mabaya mliyotenda.

decisions.choice: the negative half: a warning
decisions.reason: The two verses state the same truth from both sides, as Jewish teaching often did.

source.text: Ὅταν δὲ νηστεύητε, μὴ γίνεσθε ὡς οἱ ὑποκριταὶ σκυθρωποί, ἀφανίζουσιν γὰρ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν ὅπως φανῶσιν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύοντες· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπέχουσιν τὸν μισθὸν αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: When but you fast, not be as the hypocrites gloomy, they disfigure for the faces of them so that they may appear to the men fasting; truly I say to you, they have the reward of them.

en.L: And when you fast, do not be gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that they may appear to {{gender:people|men}} as fasting. Truly I tell you, they have their reward in full.
en.B: When you fast, do not put on a sad face as the hypocrites do. They make their faces look gloomy so that others will see they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have been paid in full.
en.R: When you go without food to pray, do not look sad like the hypocrites. They make their faces look sad so people will know they are fasting. I tell you the truth, that is all the reward they will get.

es.L: Y cuando {{plural_you:ayunen|ayunéis}}, no {{plural_you:se pongan|os pongáis}} sombríos como los hipócritas, porque desfiguran sus rostros para aparecer ante {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} como quienes ayunan. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: ya tienen cobrada su recompensa.
es.B: Cuando {{plural_you:ayunen|ayunéis}}, no {{plural_you:pongan|pongáis}} cara triste como los hipócritas. Ellos ponen la cara sombría para que los demás vean que están ayunando. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ya han recibido toda su paga.
es.R: Cuando {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} de comer para orar, no {{plural_you:pongan|pongáis}} cara triste como los hipócritas. Ellos ponen cara triste para que la gente sepa que están ayunando. {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: esa es toda la recompensa que van a recibir.

sw.L: Na mnapofunga, msiwe na nyuso za huzuni kama wanafiki, kwa maana wao huziharibu nyuso zao ili wajionyeshe kwa watu kwamba wanafunga. Kweli nawaambia, wamekwisha kupokea ujira wao wote.
sw.B: Mnapofunga, msijifanye wenye huzuni kama wanafiki. Wao hukunja nyuso zao ili wengine waone kwamba wanafunga. Kweli nawaambia, wamekwisha kulipwa kikamilifu.
sw.R: Mnapoacha kula ili kuomba, msionekane wenye huzuni kama wanafiki. Wao hujifanya kuwa na nyuso za huzuni ili watu wajue kwamba wanafunga. Nawaambia ukweli: huo ndio ujira wote watakaopata.

decisions.choice: fast: go without food for a time, as an act of devotion
decisions.reason: The law required a fast on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Devout Jews also fasted on other days; the Pharisee in Luke 18:12 fasts twice a week.

decisions.choice: disfigure ... appear: they hide their faces so that they will be seen
decisions.reason: The two verbs make a play on words: they make their faces unseen (unwashed, uncombed, perhaps with ashes) in order to be seen fasting.

decisions.choice: hypocrites: people who act a part, whose piety is a performance
decisions.reason: The word first meant a stage actor. Jesus uses it of those whose religious acts are done for an audience (6:2, 5, 16; 23:13-29).

decisions.choice: they have their reward: they have been paid in full, and there is nothing more
decisions.reason: The verb was used on receipts: "received in full". The praise of people is the whole of their reward.

decisions.choice: go without food to pray
decisions.reason: Readable says what fasting is.

source.text: σὺ δὲ νηστεύων ἄλειψαί σου τὴν κεφαλὴν καὶ τὸ πρόσωπόν σου νίψαι, ὅπως μὴ φανῇς τοῖς ἀνθρώποις νηστεύων ἀλλὰ τῷ πατρί σου τῷ ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ· καὶ ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ βλέπων ἐν τῷ κρυφαίῳ ἀποδώσει σοι.

records.literal_gloss: You but fasting anoint of you the head and the face of you wash, \v 18 so that not you may appear to the men fasting but to the Father of you the in the secret; and the Father of you the seeing in the secret will repay you.

en.L: But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face, \v 18 so that you may not appear to {{gender:people|men}} as fasting, but to your Father who [is] in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
en.B: But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face, \v 18 so that no one but your Father, who is there in secret, will know that you are fasting. Your Father sees what is hidden, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will repay you.
en.R: But when you fast, take care of your hair and wash your face, as you do every day. \v 18 Then people will not know that you are fasting. Only your Father, who is with you in secret, will know. Your Father sees what you do in secret, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will reward you.

es.L: Tú, en cambio, al ayunar, úngete la cabeza y lávate la cara, \v 18 para no aparecer ante {{gender:la gente|los hombres}} como quien ayuna, sino ante tu Padre que [está] en lo oculto; y tu Padre, que ve en lo oculto, te recompensará.
es.B: Tú, cuando ayunes, ponte aceite en el cabello y lávate la cara, \v 18 para que nadie sepa que estás ayunando, sino solo tu Padre, que está allí en lo escondido. Tu Padre ve lo escondido, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te lo pagará.
es.R: Pero cuando ayunes, arréglate el cabello y lávate la cara, como cada día. \v 18 Así la gente no sabrá que estás ayunando. Solo lo sabrá tu Padre, que está contigo en secreto. Tu Padre ve lo que haces en secreto, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te recompensará.

sw.L: Wewe lakini, unapofunga, paka kichwa chako mafuta na uoshe uso wako, \v 18 ili usijionyeshe kwa watu kwamba unafunga, bali kwa Baba yako aliye mahali pa siri; na Baba yako, anayeona yaliyo sirini, atakulipa.
sw.B: Lakini wewe unapofunga, paka mafuta kichwani na uoshe uso, \v 18 ili mtu yeyote asijue kwamba unafunga ila Baba yako, aliye pale kwa siri. Baba yako huona yaliyofichika, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakulipa.
sw.R: Lakini unapofunga, chana nywele zako na uoshe uso wako kama unavyofanya kila siku. \v 18 Hapo watu hawatajua kwamba unafunga. Ni Baba yako tu, aliye pamoja nawe kwa siri, atakayejua. Baba yako huona unachofanya kwa siri, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atakupa ujira.

decisions.choice: anoint your head and wash your face: groom yourself as on any ordinary day
decisions.reason: People put olive oil on their hair as part of daily grooming. The point is to look as usual, so that no one can tell.

decisions.choice: your Father who sees in secret will reward you: God sees and gives what he has promised
alternatives: a wage earned by the act
decisions.reason: What is done for God alone is seen by him. The reward is his gift, in this life and at the last day (6:20; 25:34-40).

decisions.choice: take care of your hair, as you do every day
decisions.reason: Anointing is unfamiliar as grooming; Readable says what it meant.
